newsitem.title: USA: NFL-EAGLES QB PEETE HAS SEASON-ENDING KNEE SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: NFL-EAGLES QB PEETE HAS SEASON-ENDING KNEE SURGERY.

text.p: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Rodney Peete underwent season-ending knee surgery Tuesday to repair the devastating knee injury he suffered in Monday night's loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Peete was simply dropping back to pass during the second quarter when he caught his cleats in the Veteran's Stadium turf. He ruptured his right patella tendon and collapsed to the field, his season over.
"The prognosis is that he should recover fully," said team physician Dr. Arthur Bartolozzi, who performed the surgery.
"It is quite a devastating and serious injury, so it could take some time to recover. We expect him to rehab over the next six to nine months," Bartolozzi said.
"The tendon is the structure that connects the kneecap to the tibia. The tear, in this case, completely separates the kneecap from the lower leg."
Peete had completed 9-of-16 passes for 98 yards and one interception before being carted off the field.
The Eagles starter completed 80-for-134 passes for 992 yards with three touchdowns and five interceptions for his abreviated season.
Backup Ty Detmer replaced Peete to finish the Eagles' 23-19 defeat.

Philadelphia head coach Ray Rhodes told ESPN that Detmer suffered a concussion in Monday's game but would be the starter when the Eagles (3-2) meet the New York Giants on October 13. Philadelphia has a bye this week.
The only other quarterback on the roster is rookie Bobby Hoying, leaving Rhodes in the market for an experienced quarterback to run his offence.

Rhodes said the club plans to bring in Mark Rypien on Wednesday for a physical and a workout. Rypien, who led the Washington Redskins to victory in Super Bowl XXVI, was cut by the St Louis Rams in training camp.
